stumbles.quote: Yes. A life-sciences vocabulary makes Ettin cheaper on PubMed text, but only when the pre-tokenizer stops splitting biomedical terms.
stumbles.why: The answer is stated as a general yes, but the evidence is one 50K retrained BPE on 39,000 abstracts. "Cheaper" is only defined as token count, not compute or cost, until the last paragraph.

stumbles.quote: Retraining the vocabulary on its own is therefore not enough to get the saving.
stumbles.why: It sits awkwardly with the 8% saving from retraining alone, since the text doesn't say whether 8% counts as a worthwhile saving.

point: On PubMed abstracts, a 50K BPE vocabulary retrained with whitespace-only pre-tokenization needs about 21% fewer tokens than Ettin's tokenizer, and most of that gain comes from changing the pre-tokenizer rather than from retraining the vocabulary (8%).
